subject: fix(team): delegate agent profiles without crashing or leaking prompt text
instruction:
fix(team): delegate agent profiles without crashing or leaking prompt text

`portable_request?/1` reached its `is_map/1` clause with an `%Ouroboros.AgentProfile{}`
and raised `Protocol.UndefinedError` (a struct has no `Enumerable`). The rescue then
built `{:invalid_delegation_options, Exception.message(error)}` from the raising term,
so every delegation carrying a profile failed *and* embedded the whole profile —
base prompt, instructions, tool descriptions — in the returned and checkpointed error.

Decompose structs before the map clause, mirroring `Interactive.State.serializable?/1`,
and report only the exception type: this function only ever inspects prompt text.

A delegated task also lost its prompt identity. `TaskState`'s request options drop
`:agent_profile` and keep only the compiled prompt, so the owner received that text as
a *session* prompt, wrapped it a second time, and produced a task with `prompt_trace:
nil` and no `metadata.ouroboros_prompt`. The assembler's inputs now travel beside the
compiled options as `coding_options.prompt_inputs`, never inside them: assembly is
deterministic, so the owner reproduces byte-identical options — which is what
`verified_coding_task/1` compares — plus the same trace the local task would have.

Redaction turns every struct it walks into a plain map, so the secret-bearing check
now compares the same struct-free projection redaction itself would produce.

The deterministic test adapter accepts the normalized prompt options, without which
no test provider could exercise an assembled profile end to end.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a delegated agent profile keeps the prompt identity of the identical local task
  - delegation errors carry no profile or prompt text

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
